% SCI-PTC v0.1 shared normative equations -- owner-review draft r0.4.
\section{Normative equations}
\label{sec:normative-equations}

The organizing detector-time model separates the latent correlated component
from its fitted estimate:
\begin{equation}
Y^{\rm CAL}_{td}=S_{td}+U_{\star,td}+N_{td},
\qquad
U_{\star,td}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}M_{\star,tk}A_{\star,dk}.
\label{eq:ptc-model}
\end{equation}
For the immutable fitted parent, the realized modeled component and transformed
signal satisfy the identity
\begin{equation}
\widehat U=\widehat M\widehat A^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
Z=\mathcal A_{\Theta}(Y^{\rm CAL})
  =Y^{\rm CAL}-\widehat U.
\label{eq:ptc-subtraction}
\end{equation}
Equation~\ref{eq:ptc-subtraction} states the realized result on the fitted
parent. It does not define how a new input or response companion is applied.

For declared learned additive location $\lambda$ and invertible internal
scaling $D$, the fitting coordinate and physical-unit application map are
\begin{equation}
Y'_c=C_{\lambda}(Y')=Y'-\lambda,
\qquad
\widetilde Y'=D^{-1}Y'_c,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\Theta}(Y')
=D\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\Theta}(\widetilde Y').
\label{eq:center-scale}
\end{equation}
Scaling is restored for ordinary output; $\lambda$ is not. Detector $x$ has
no scientifically meaningful optical DC response, so the removed additive
reference is discarded and published in $\mathcal N_{\rm PTC}$. In
fixed-state application $\lambda$ is held fixed. In a full-procedure response
it is re-estimated in each run, may move under perturbation, and is again
discarded.

Facts and causes accumulate without erasure, while admission is a separate
owner-controlled decision for an exact named use:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C&=\bigcup_i\mathcal C_i,\\
\operatorname{eligible}_U
  &=b_U\land\bigwedge_{i\in I_U}p_{i,U},\\
\operatorname{ineligible}_U
  &=\bigvee_{i\in I_U}\neg p_{i,U}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:cause-support}
\end{equation}
One applicable exclusion cannot be rescued by another cause. If no known
predicate excludes the occurrence but any required predicate is unknown, the
result is \texttt{decision\_unavailable}, not eligible. PTC owns this rule for
PTC-local uses; another named-use owner supplies its own policy while
consuming the preserved facts.

An admitted weighted or robust low-rank family minimizes
\begin{equation}
(\widehat M,\widehat A)=
\arg\min_{M,A}\sum_{t,d}w^{\rm fit}_{td}
\,\rho\!\left(\widetilde Y_{td}-(MA^{\mathsf T})_{td}\right),
\label{eq:masked-factor}
\end{equation}
where $w^{\rm fit}_{td}=0$ denotes no fit influence, not a zero-valued
observation. The loss, metric, support, rank, and missing-data semantics are
declared.

For a fixed supplied design $B$ and fit metric $\Omega$, a conditioned
regression family is
\begin{equation}
\widehat c=(B^{\mathsf T}\Omega B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\Omega y,
\qquad
\mathcal L_{B,\Omega}
=I-B(B^{\mathsf T}\Omega B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\Omega .
\label{eq:fixed-regression}
\end{equation}
The generalized inverse, tolerance, units, gauge, coefficient support, and
application support are material state.

A weighted common-mode family may estimate its temporal mode as
\begin{equation}
\widehat m_t=
\frac{\sum_d w^{\rm fit}_{td}\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}
      \widetilde Y_{td}}
     {\sum_d w^{\rm fit}_{td}\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}},
\label{eq:common-mode}
\end{equation}
only where the denominator is finite and nonzero. The aggregation weight
$\omega^{\rm cm}_{td}$, its unit, normalization, and population are declared;
it is not a fitted detector loading by implication.

For base-v0.1 PCA/SVD, application means projection of any admitted
application input through the frozen realized subspace and metric:
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\Theta}(\widetilde Y')=
\begin{cases}
\mathcal L^{t}_{\Theta}\widetilde Y',
  &\text{temporal-space left action},\\
\widetilde Y'\mathcal L^{d}_{\Theta},
  &\text{detector-space right action},\\
\operatorname{unvec}\!\left[
\mathcal L^{v}_{\Theta}\operatorname{vec}(\widetilde Y')\right],
  &\text{declared vectorized action}.
\end{cases}
\label{eq:conditional-cleaner}
\end{equation}
The realized family selects exactly one compatible action and records its
domain, codomain, metric, supports, generalized inverse/tolerance, and
linear coefficient-recomputation rule. A two-sided or detector/time-specific
action is represented by its exact vectorized operator; it is not inferred
from matrix orientation or rank alone.

A separately named frozen-component subtraction family is
\begin{equation}
\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U}(Y')=Y'-\widehat U,
\qquad
D\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U}[Y](H)=H.
\label{eq:frozen-component}
\end{equation}
It is not interchangeable with Equation~\ref{eq:conditional-cleaner} and is
not the base-v0.1 PCA/SVD application rule.

A declared within-array hierarchical model may be written
\begin{equation}
U_\star=U_\star^{\rm array}+U_\star^{\rm network}+U_\star^{\rm local},
\label{eq:hierarchy}
\end{equation}
with exact group identities and joint or sequential fit order. Sequential
fitting publishes the complete ordered composition and cumulative response.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite candidate set with declared order $\preceq$. The
base selection rule is
\begin{equation}
c_{\star}=\min_{\preceq}\left\{c\in\mathcal C:
P_{\rm corr}(c)\wedge P_{\rm sky}(c)\wedge P_{\rm cond}(c)
\wedge P_{\rm supp}(c)\wedge P_{\rm stab}(c)\wedge P_{\rm QC}(c)
\right\}.
\label{eq:conjunctive-selection}
\end{equation}
Every predicate value, unit, threshold, uncertainty treatment, pass/fail
cause, order, tie, and rejected candidate is retained in $\mathfrak L$.

For refinement index $j$, the support-changing lifecycle is
\begin{align}
\Theta_j&=\operatorname{Fit}(Y^{\rm CAL};\mathcal S_j),\nonumber\\
\mathcal S_{j+1}&=\operatorname{Classify}(Y^{\rm CAL},\Theta_j),\nonumber\\
\Theta_{j+1}&=\operatorname{Fit}(Y^{\rm CAL};\mathcal S_{j+1}).
\label{eq:immutable-refit}
\end{align}
Every fit uses the same immutable admitted CAL parent. A cleaned $Z_j$ is not
the next fit parent, and the final complete model is applied once.

The one-way state lifecycle is
\begin{equation}
R\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow O\longrightarrow
\mathfrak L\longrightarrow\Theta\longrightarrow\Lambda\longrightarrow\Pi ,
\label{eq:lifecycle}
\end{equation}
where learned evidence, resolved selection, numerical application, and
publication are distinct immutable states.

The full PTC procedure has separately typed signal and state projections:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal P(Y^{\rm CAL},R,E,O)
=\bigl(\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL}),\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL})\bigr)
=(Z,\Lambda).
\label{eq:full-procedure}
\end{equation}

For fixed resolved model $\Theta$, including frozen $\lambda$, the local
detector-time response and a realized CAL-grid companion are
\begin{equation}
J_{\Theta}[Y]=D\mathcal A_{\Theta}[Y],
\qquad
k_{\rm src}^{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}
=J_{\Theta}[Y]\,k_{\rm src}^{\rm CAL}.
\label{eq:local-companion}
\end{equation}
If the parent is source-domain, the complete chain response is
\begin{equation}
k_{\rm src}^{\rm CAL}=K_{\rm up\to CAL}\tau_{\rm src},
\qquad
K_{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}=J_{\Theta}[Y]\circ K_{\rm up\to CAL},
\qquad
k_{\rm src}^{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}
=K_{\rm PTC\mid\Theta}\tau_{\rm src}.
\label{eq:conditional-response}
\end{equation}
Equations~\ref{eq:local-companion}--\ref{eq:conditional-response} are
alternative entry points for different companion parents;
$K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ is
never applied twice.

For a declared detector-time perturbation $h^{\rm CAL}$, the full-procedure
finite-perturbation signal response is
\begin{equation}
K_{\rm PTC}^{\rm proc}(\epsilon,h^{\rm CAL})=
\frac{\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL}+\epsilon h^{\rm CAL})
      -\mathcal P_Z(Y^{\rm CAL})}{\epsilon}.
\label{eq:e2e-response}
\end{equation}
Each full-procedure evaluation re-estimates and again discards $\lambda$. The
corresponding state evidence, including any centering-state movement, is
retained separately:
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm state}(\epsilon,h^{\rm CAL})=
\operatorname{Compare}_{\rm typed}\!\left[
\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL}+\epsilon h^{\rm CAL}),
\mathcal P_{\Lambda}(Y^{\rm CAL})\right].
\label{eq:e2e-state}
\end{equation}
Amplitude, side, source state, location, domain, and every changed rank, mask,
group, support, class, convergence, or fallback field are part of the result.

For response role $r\in\{\mathrm{fixed},\mathrm{procedure}\}$, the optional
map-center diagnostic is
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\rm center}^{\,r}
=e_{\rm center}^{\mathsf T}A_{\rm ref}k_{\rm src}^{\rm PTC,r}.
\label{eq:map-center}
\end{equation}
The exact response role, source-companion parent, reference MAP operator, and
center selector are mandatory factors. The diagnostic confers no MAP or
general beam authority.

For a fixed differentiable realized map, conditional covariance is
\begin{equation}
C_{Z\mid\Theta}=J_{\Theta}[Y]\,C_Y\,J_{\Theta}[Y]^{\mathsf T}.
\label{eq:conditional-covariance}
\end{equation}
For random selected state $\Theta$, the exact decomposition is
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Cov}(Z)=
\operatorname{E}\!\left[\operatorname{Cov}(Z\mid\Theta)\right]
+\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\operatorname{E}[Z\mid\Theta]\right).
\label{eq:total-covariance}
\end{equation}
Omitting the second term is a conditioned approximation, not complete
uncertainty.

A diagnostic indexed by detector or detector-time occurrence may take the
generic residual form
\begin{equation}
\eta_i=H_i(Z,\widehat U,\mathcal S,\Theta;\chi_H),
\label{eq:diagnostic}
\end{equation}
where $\chi_H$ records the domain, population/model reference, normalization,
support, uncertainty, and policy role.

A downstream analysis/gridding coefficient family is
\begin{equation}
\widetilde\gamma_i=f_{\gamma}(\eta_i;\chi_{\gamma}),
\qquad
\gamma_i=
\mathcal N_{\gamma}\!\left(
\widetilde\gamma_i;\{\widetilde\gamma_j:j\in\mathcal D_{\gamma}\}\right),
\label{eq:analysis-coefficient}
\end{equation}
where $i=d$ or $i=(t,d)$ is declared, $\mathcal D_{\gamma}$ is the exact
normalization domain, and $f_{\gamma}$ and $\mathcal N_{\gamma}$ are named
operators. The result is not precision unless separately proved.

Transitive causal influence for output $j$ is
\begin{equation}
\mathcal I_j=\bigcup_{i:\,i\rightarrow j}
\left(\{i\}\cup\mathcal I_i\right),
\label{eq:influence}
\end{equation}
including inputs that affect fitted state or selection even when a local
numeric derivative vanishes.

For disabled PTC on the PTC-dependent route,
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{PTC}=\mathsf{disabled}
\Longrightarrow
\mathsf{Exist}_{p}=\mathsf{disabled}
\quad
\text{for }p\in\{Z,\Lambda,\gamma,\mathsf{MAP}_{\rm PTC-route}\}.
\label{eq:disabled-route}
\end{equation}
This product-realization statement does not assign response availability and
does not govern a separately authorized direct CAL-to-MAP route.
